build: Supplied Black Label original G64 disk engine; Gray, Yellow and Official Cartridge Image CRT compared separately

exclude: Loader, KERNAL workspace and engine-generated sprites, map grids, row addresses, sector buffers and working variables
Unloaded tail and generated title/play/work bitmaps
Not loaded by IT: runtime sound queues, score scratch, system I/O and RAM beneath KERNAL ROM
150 parts: Room 1, Room 10, Room 100 and others
extra: Loaded DB title bitmap RLE data
Entire loaded IT engine, tables, sounds, graphics and demonstration rooms
elsewhere: 150 parts: Room 1, Room 10, Room 100 and others

comments.text: First 512 count/value records of DB, expanded by the loop at $62E5 in draw_title ($628A). Starting from cursor $1FFF, these records write $2000-$2BE7; the complete decoder stops when the cursor high byte reaches $3F.
Next 512 count/value records in the title stream. They continue the same expansion cursor and write $2BE8-$36E7 before the final records at $1C00.
Final 306 records actually consumed by the title decoder. The 1330th record advances the output cursor to $3F56, ending the loop at $6312; compressed input ends at $1E63.

155 bytes loaded with DB after its consumed RLE stream. The title decoder has already stopped before this address; they are retained file contents, not a further displayed run. Other uses remain a verification question.

Black Label loader hand-over. Set sound enable to zero, initialize machine tables/vectors and probe original-disk sectors, then invoke the score-sector helper before resetting options and drawing the title. Its transfer follows the inherited game mode: the original cold-entry RAM has mode zero, so this invocation takes the demo-copy path rather than reading the drive score sector.

Reset sound/effect state, input history, display options and mode; set the pacing threshold to five and joystick input selector to $CA, then draw the title. This entry does not initialize the lives counter; start_new_game ($605E) sets five lives.

Clear four score bytes, difficulty cycle, previous-room flag and demo duration; initialize the demo script cursor to $B100 and lives to five. Preserve displayed level and physical room index supplied by the caller, select the live bitmap and construct that room.

Load and decode the room, reset the music queue and drill controls, and enable the player plus zero to five guards. Modes with $1306>>1 nonzero flash the runner until key or joystick input. Select three guard masks using the unchecked sum of difficulty cycle and guard count, and read the trap threshold before main_loop.

Call update_runner, then test alive. A zero gold counter queues the completion motif and activates exit ladders. At row zero/fine-Y two, a zero or $FF gold counter completes the room; otherwise update holes and guards, checking alive after each. Wait for the IRQ counter to reach the pacing threshold, reset it to three, and repeat.

Increment displayed and physical level indexes, wait until music head equals tail, and advance the motif cycle. Award an extra life with saturation at $FF, then run fifteen voice-1 frequency steps with interrupts masked; each step adds 100 points, for a 1500-point completion bonus. Start the next room.

Decrement lives. Modes zero and one return through the saved attract-sound operand immediately. Other modes start the $38 death sweep, wait for queued music, clear drilling and redraw lives, then wait for the sweep to end. Retry while lives remain; at zero, process eligible high scores and return to attract input.

Poll port-2 fire and the IRQ-produced key latch. Editor and score-view keys dispatch their modes; a delay cycles the title, three demonstration boards and the score screen. Fire or another start key selects a new game.
Self-modified immediate byte in LDA at $622E. Attract setup saves the sound-enabled byte here and demo exit restores it.
Set physical room index zero and displayed level one, mark score eligibility, enable sound and select mode two, then initialize a new run.

Eleven aligned offsets 0,3,...,30 into guard-update masks at $7B83. Setup indexes this base with difficulty cycle plus guard count without clamping the sum; indexes 11..15 therefore read the following trap-threshold bytes.

Twenty-one nondecreasing trap-state thresholds, beginning with two copies of $26. Automatic room wrapping caps the difficulty cycle at ten, so that path reads the first eleven thresholds. The first five bytes also alias guard-schedule offsets for unchecked cycle+guardcount indexes11..15.

Clear the display bitmap, select high-resolution bitmap mode and its title colour bands, then expand DB count/value records from $1400 into the bitmap. Returns to the attract loop after the output cursor reaches page $3F.

Read queue duration and two pitches. The loaded control byte is overwritten by $F0, masked with sound enable, before writing voice-2/3 sustain/release. A negative harmony value computes voice-three frequency as voice-two frequency minus $0080. Tick duration and advance the head; empty queues clear the voice controls.

Pull the call return address and advance it to inline four-byte events: duration, voice-2 pitch, voice-3 pitch/flag, and a fourth payload byte. Append events to the four-page ring until zero duration, then resume after the sentinel. The fourth byte is stored in $C300 but is ignored by music_queue_tick, which overwrites its load with $F0.

A supplies the minimum absolute difference from the previously accepted low raster byte; X and Y supply inclusive lower and upper raster limits. Wait for an acceptable $D012 value, store it at $1335 and return that line in A. The four callers at $7A73/$7A7B/$7A83/$7A8B sample pitches during gold pickup.
Load the starting motif countdown and semitone offset from $9500/$9501 into $1332/$1333.

Decrement the motif countdown. A nonnegative result returns without changing the pitch offset; a negative result advances that offset, wraps it to $9501 when it reaches $9502, and reloads the countdown from $9500. With the loaded countdown nine, transposition changes after ten calls.

Use twice the motif countdown at $1332 to select a little-endian stream pointer from $9503/$9504. Add $1333 to nonzero voice-2 pitches and positive harmony pitches, leaving zero and negative harmony unchanged. Append four-byte events until zero duration; the queue tick adds no further transposition.

Increment the pacing counter, write sound-enabled master volume and the voice-1 effect frequency high byte, and tick the music queue. Convert the previous KERNAL key result into a new-key latch: remap key zero to seven, tag any modifier with bit seven, and suppress unchanged keys until a no-key scan resets the history. Chain to $EA31 for the next scan/system tick.

Clear LORAM in $01, generate 200 bitmap row-offset entries at $0E00/$0F00, and install IRQ $648A plus NMI $65CF. Set voice-1 sustain/release and triangle/gate control, sprite pointers and colours. Clear $0002-$0101 and $0C00-$0DFF, then enable all sprite slots.

Save A in the immediate colour operand at $65B0 and enable multicolour mode. One 256-iteration loop performs four screen stores per iteration, filling $0400-$07F7: 1000 visible cells plus sixteen padding bytes, with eight overlapping stores. The same loop fills all 1024 bytes $D800-$DBFF with colour one. Sprite pointers $07F8-$07FF are preserved.
Immediate operand of LDA at $65AF, rewritten by fill_screen_colours and read by temporary-message callers to restore the previous fill.
The installed NMI target is a single RTI: RESTORE does not enter the default KERNAL recovery handler.
Six sprite-enable bytes for zero through five guards: $01,$05,$0D,$1D,$5D,$DD. The player uses slot zero; guards use slots 2,3,4,6,7.

Clear score bytes, set five lives and editor mode, preserve the previous input selector in a later immediate operand, and draw the board-editor menu. Physical board selection is limited to the 150-board data set.

Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6620: LODE RUNNER BOARD EDITOR / ---------------------------- /  R/S KEY ABORTS ANY COMMAND. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6678.

Print COMMAND>, wait for a KERNAL matrix key and search the six editor command codes. The matching table word is pushed as a return address, so RTS dispatches to that word plus one; unmatched keys sound an error.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $667E: COMMAND>. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $668B.
Continuation after COMMAND>: read the key latch and dispatch the matching six-command RTS word, or beep and prompt again.
KERNAL key numbers for P,C,E,M,I,S followed by a zero sentinel. The command prompt selects the corresponding RTS-dispatch word.
Six little-endian handler addresses minus one, for play, clear, edit, move, initialize and clear-scores. The prompt pushes the selected word and RTS increments it to the real handler.
High-byte base of editor_command_returns. Indexed loads pair it with the low-byte base when pushing the six RTS return words.

Print PLAY LEVEL, then read a board number and load the previously saved input selector from the self-modified immediate operand at $66D7. Enter mode three; starting beyond room one clears score eligibility.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $66C0: >>PLAY LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $66D1.
After PLAY LEVEL text, read the numeric board, restore the saved input selector through $66D7, set mode three and eligibility only for physical room zero, then initialize play.
Immediate value of LDA at $66D6. board_editor_menu patches this with the previous joystick/keyboard selector; selected-board play restores it before constructing the room.
Read a board number and require a valid user disk. Clear the 256-byte packed-sector buffer and write that board, returning to the command prompt.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $66F8: >>CLEAR LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $670A.
After CLEAR LEVEL text, require a valid board number and user disk, zero the packed 256-byte sector and write it. Abort returns to the editor error/prompt path.
Read a board number and enter the cell editor; rejected or aborted numeric input returns to the error/prompt path.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6726: >>EDIT LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6737.
After EDIT LEVEL text, a valid numeric selection enters edit_board; carry indicates abort/invalid selection.

Read source and destination board numbers, acknowledge each disk prompt, and require a recognized user disk for both. Read the source sector into $1000, then write that buffer to the destination board and return to the editor prompt.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6742: >>MOVE LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6753.
Read and save the source board index, print TO LEVEL and continue with destination selection.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $675B: TO LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6768.
Read and save the destination board, then print the source-disk prompt.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6770: SOURCE DISKETTE. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6786.
After source prompt acknowledgement, validate the disk and read the source board into the sector buffer. Print the destination-disk prompt.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6797: DESTINATION DISKETTE. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $67B2.
After destination acknowledgement, validate that disk and write the buffered source board to the selected destination index, then return to the editor command prompt.
Ask for Y before preparing a formatted disk. A master-disk marker blocks this path. Otherwise call sector_io with mode four to zero all 150 room sectors and write the user-disk score marker.

Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $67C9: >>INITIALIZE /   THIS PREPARES AN ALREADY /   FORMATTED DISK FOR USER /   CREATED LEVELS. /   (WILL DESTROY OLD DATA). /  /   ARE YOU SURE (Y/N). Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6853.
After the initialization warning, read Y/N, require Y and reject a master marker. Prepare the 150 room sectors and user score marker, then return to the prompt.
Ask for Y, validate the score-sector signature and clear its first 128 bytes before writing it back. This operation is allowed on either master or user data disks.

Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6879: >>CLEAR SCORE FILE /   THIS CLEARS THE HIGH /   SCORE FILE OF ALL /   ENTRIES. /  /   ARE YOU SURE (Y/N). Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $68DD.
After the score-clear warning, accept Y, require a recognized Lode Runner disk and clear the first 128 score-sector bytes. Write the score sector and return to the prompt.

Require a user disk, render the selected board into the work bitmap and initialize the cursor. Numeric keys replace a grid cell and clear the saved flag when it changes; other keys use the editor dispatch directory.

Preserve cursor coordinates, read the disk marker and reject invalid or master disks. Pack the 28-by-16 grid into a 256-byte sector, write it and mark the board saved; rejection reconstructs the editor display.

Return immediately if the saved flag is set. Otherwise display a confirmation screen, accept Y/N through the same key latch and call save_edited_board for Y, then restore the previous screen colour fill.

Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6A19: LEVEL HAS BEEN CHANGED BUT / NOT SAVED. DO YOU WISH TO / SAVE MODIFIED LEVEL (Y/N). Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6A6C.
Beep and wait for Y/N. Y calls save_edited_board; N skips it. Restore the saved colour-fill value and return to the caller.
Read and check the score-sector signature. An invalid marker displays the data-disk warning; the master marker displays the editing refusal. Only a recognized user disk returns normally.
Temporarily replace the board with the master-disk manipulation warning, wait for a key, then reconstruct the room bitmap and restore the previous fill colour.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6AB8: USER NOT ALLOWED TO / MANIPULATE MASTER DISKETTE.. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6AEB.
Print HIT A KEY TO CONTINUE following the master-disk warning. Its inline text resumes at acknowledge_disk_warning.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6AEB: HIT A KEY TO CONTINUE. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6B07.
Beep, wait for a key, consume the latch and reconstruct the board in the work bitmap; restore the saved colour-fill byte before returning.
Display the invalid Lode Runner disk warning, then share the acknowledgement and board-redraw path with show_master_disk_refusal.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6B3D: DISKETTE IN DRIVE IS NOT A / LODE RUNNER DATA DISK.. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6B72.
Jump to the shared acknowledgement prompt after the invalid-data-disk text.
Read the current cell through the logical-grid row directory and flash it with the input-wait cursor routine.
Eight raw key-latch codes followed by a zero sentinel. They select cursor movement, save, next/previous board and quit through cell_editor_command_returns.
Eight interleaved handler addresses minus one. Resolve them by adding one after reading the little-endian words; these targets are code and are explicitly traced.
High-byte base of cell_editor_command_returns; paired indexed reads dispatch the eight movement/save/navigation commands.

Display and edit three decimal digits, initially the physical room index plus one. On Return, reject arithmetic overflow with carry set; otherwise store the displayed number at $1305 and its decremented index at $1310/Y before testing Y<$96. Carry clear therefore accepts exactly boards 1..150. Run/Stop jumps to the editor prompt instead of returning.
Flash a blank cursor until a key or stick input appears, consume the IRQ key latch and map Run/Stop to the main editor prompt.
Four loaded zero bytes used at runtime for the decimal cursor, saved text column, source board and destination board. Initial values have no persistent score or level meaning.
Saved text column for the three-digit board-number cursor. Following bytes preserve source/destination board indexes for MOVE.
Saved zero-based source board for MOVE; the next byte stores destination. These loaded bytes are runtime scratch, not persistent room data.
Saved zero-based destination board for MOVE, used after its disk prompt/validation.
Consume $1328 and compare it with the ten key codes in $6C98. A matching digit returns its index with carry clear; other commands keep their raw key code and set carry.
KERNAL matrix key numbers for digits zero through nine; consume_numeric_key returns the matching index as the tile/digit value.
Eleven high-bit PETSCII bytes spelling DANE BIGHAM. read_or_write_score_sector checks these at $11F0-$11FA to recognize a Lode Runner data disk.

Skip disqualified or zero-score runs. Read the score sector, compare displayed level first and then packed-BCD score bytes, shift eight-byte entries down, and accept three initials. Write the edited sector only if a second read still matches its saved pre-edit copy.

Low address byte of indexed LDA at $6D7D, patched with the selected eight-byte record offset. The continuation accepts three initials, rereads the sector and writes only when it still matches the saved original.

Low address byte of STA at $6DC9, patched to the chosen score-record offset together with the initials read. Input accepts letters, space and period; after Return, reread the sector and retain changes only if the saved original matches.
Clear the bitmap and print the high-score heading, then draw ten eight-byte records from the score-sector buffer. Each record carries three initials, displayed level and four packed-BCD score bytes.

Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $6E20: LODE RUNNER HIGH SCORES /  /  /     INITIALS LEVEL  SCORE /     -------- ----- --------. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $6E78.
After the score heading, start rank one. Print ranks 1..9 with a leading blank and rank ten as two digits, followed by an inline punctuation gap.
Inline high-bit PETSCII argument to print_inline_text ($88F4), called at $6E97: one period followed by four spaces. A zero at $6E9F terminates the text; execution resumes at $6EA0.
Find the eight-byte record for the displayed rank. A zero level skips the empty row; otherwise print three initials and an inline gap before its displayed level.
Inline high-bit PETSCII argument to print_inline_text ($88F4), called at $6EC7: four spaces. A zero at $6ECE terminates the gap; execution resumes at $6ECF.
After the initials gap, print the record level byte as three binary decimal digits, then the inline gap before score.
Inline high-bit PETSCII argument to print_inline_text ($88F4), called at $6EE9: two spaces. A zero at $6EEE terminates the gap; execution resumes at $6EEF.
Read the four score bytes in their big-endian record order and draw each pair of BCD nibbles. Advance to a new row and continue through rank ten.
Offsets 0,0,8,...,72 let one-based ranks address ten eight-byte records in the score sector. The duplicate first zero accommodates the one-based callers.

Map raw latch code $82 (shifted cursor-right, meaning cursor-left) to key-table index seven. Otherwise use A unchanged as the index into $6F66 and set bit seven on the result. There is no general masking or bounds check for other modifier-tagged codes.
64-entry KERNAL matrix-order conversion table. Letters and digits map to ASCII before the caller sets bit seven; unsupported/function/modifier keys use $FF.

Reset per-room actor, gold, exit and hole state, clearing all 31 timer cells $12E0-$12FE. Read the selected sector unless its index matches the cache, and unpack exactly $1000-$10DF as 448 cells low nibble first through row directories into dynamic and backing grids; values ten through fifteen become blank. Render/extract according to input X. If a play room lacks a runner, a nonzero index retries board zero and raises the automatic difficulty cycle up to ten; board zero without a runner resets to the title.

Read the logical 28-by-16 grid row-major. Store even-index cells in the low nibble and odd-index cells in the high nibble of the 224-byte payload, leaving the sector tail intact, then write through sector_io.

A=1 reads, A=2 writes and A=4 prepares a user disk. With bit seven set, strip that bit and use the already prepared track/sector digits, bypassing demo selection and digit calculation. Otherwise modes zero/one copy embedded demo sectors $B500-$B7FF; live/editor modes calculate track=3+index/16 and sector=index mod16, use DOS U1/U2 via channels15/2, and transfer 256 bytes.
High address byte of the embedded-demo sector LDA, computed from $B5 plus the room index.

Save the room index and increment the disk-transfer page operands $71FF/$7219 to select $1100. With ordinary read/write requests in modes two or higher, temporary index $97 selects track12, sector7. Modes zero/one instead take the embedded-demo path, which copies to $1000 and can advance the difficulty cycle; it does not fill $1100. Restore the saved index and page operands, then compare all eleven existing marker bytes $11F0-$11FA with $6CA2. Return A=0 for an invalid marker, A=1 for a valid marker with nonzero $11FB, or A=$FF when $11FB is zero.

Discard one CHRIN result before the storing loop at $71FA. In the supplied room sectors, raw byte zero is skipped: the 224-byte grid payload is raw offsets 1 through 224, loaded at $1000-$10DF. The storing loop still performs 256 reads; the skipped byte's protocol purpose is not established.
High address byte of the indexed sector-read store. Normally $10 for board buffer $1000; score transfer patches it to $11. The following instructions continue the 256-byte transfer and finalization.
High address byte of the indexed sector-write load, paired with the read operand. Score I/O temporarily changes this from $10 to $11.
A zero byte followed by #, the one-byte filename used to open a direct-access drive buffer. The zero is retained immediately before that filename.
Zero-terminated U1/U2 command text for drive channel 15. Mutable ASCII digits select track/sector and the first digit selects read versus write; carriage return executes it.
Mutable ASCII 1/2 in the DOS U1/U2 command. Sector I/O chooses read or write by patching this command byte.
Mutable ASCII track and sector digits inside dos_sector_command. The following U+ finalization string is separate; room index division by sixteen supplies these numbers.
Mutable ASCII track units digit in the U1/U2 command, following the tens digit. The remaining text includes mutable sector digits and carriage-return terminator.
Mutable ASCII sector tens digit. The following units digit, carriage return and zero complete the DOS U1/U2 command; sector_io derives the number from room index modulo sixteen.
Mutable ASCII sector units digit, followed by carriage return and zero terminating the U1/U2 DOS sector command. The tens/units pair is patched from the physical room index modulo sixteen.
U+ followed by carriage return and a zero terminator, sent after each sector transfer before closing the channels.

Read two DOS status bytes, OR them, consume through carriage return and accept when their OR is $30. For ordinary ASCII decimal status digits this accepts only 00; across all byte pairs, nine satisfy this test. Otherwise jump to the reset/title path.
Restore default channels, send U+ followed by carriage return to the command channel, then close all files through KERNAL $FFE7.

Draw 448 cells into the $4000 work bitmap through row directories. With $1300 nonzero, count gold, erase hidden ladder markers while recording at most45, and initialize at mostfive guards plus one runner. Retain actor markers in the dynamic grid, blank them in the backing grid, and erase excess actors from both. Trapdoor code five draws as brick one. With $1300 zero, preserve and draw all editor markers, then copy work to display; successful play also removes retained actor pictures from work after the reveal/copy.

Transition-disabled path: select the work text target, draw its status bar at $86E1, copy all8192 bytes $4000-$5FFF to display $2000-$3FFF through $735E, and select the display text target. Continue by erasing actor pictures from work. The animated path is the separate $7395 call to $90EC.

Set contact vulnerability for this pass. Continue a pending drill; otherwise test ladder/bar/floor support and apply gravity before reading movement. A falling runner erases its old picture, advances one fine-Y phase and redraws its sprite; only a phase wrap restores the vacated dynamic cell and marks the next row. Supported input tries vertical/drill first, then horizontal.

When fine-X is below three, reject the left edge or dynamic-cell codes one, two and five to the left. Otherwise erase the old runner, move fine-Y toward center, face left and decrement fine-X; a cell crossing restores the old dynamic cell from backing terrain (brick becomes blank) and writes runner code nine into the new cell. Cycle walking/bar frames, check centered gold and redraw. This routine does not provide a consistent blocked-move carry result.
Rightward partner of runner_move_left, bounded at column 27. Cell crossing changes logical occupancy, fine-X wraps over five phases, and centered gold pickup shares the runner collision/drawing path.

Require ladder support in the current backing cell, or below it when fine-Y is at least three. For a current ladder with fine-Y below three, reject row zero and dynamic-cell codes one, two or five above. Move fine-X toward center, step upward through five fine-Y phases, update dynamic occupancy and cycle climb frames. Carry set rejects; clear reports success. Top-row completion is tested separately in main_loop at $6133-$6140.

For fine-Y at least two, reject row fifteen or dynamic-cell codes one/two below; lower fine-Y phases skip that test. Move fine-X toward center, step down through five fine-Y phases, update dynamic occupancy and use the shared climb frames/redraw path. Carry set rejects and clear reports success. This routine contains no ladder/bar prerequisite.

Set a negative drill flag and phase zero. Require a brick diagonally below-left, room bounds and a blank neighboring cell beside the runner. Each continuation aligns the runner, updates spray/brick glyphs and advances the phase; phase 12 completes the hole, while an obstruction cancels it. Completion takes 13 successful runner updates including the start; the phase-12 call allocates after twelve increments.

Set a positive drill flag and phase 12. Apply the mirrored below-right brick and blank-neighbor checks; animated phases 12..23 use the right half of the spray table and the corresponding brick-erasure animation. Phase 24 completes the hole and calls finish_dug_hole with the right column. Completion takes 13 successful runner updates including the start; the phase-24 call allocates after twelve increments.

First sixteen entries of the eighteen-entry runner frame-to-glyph mapping, used for walking, hanging, drilling and falling. Climbing frame indexes sixteen/seventeen continue into the two bytes at $7875-$7876.

Final two runner-frame glyphs, $0E/$12, used by climbing animation indexes sixteen and seventeen from the table base $7865. The second byte at $7876 also names the previous-spray base alias; it is not an unused retained glyph.

Previous-spray base alias, also the second climbing glyph byte. Left drill phases1..11 and right phases13..23 index it to erase the preceding spray-table entry. The initial left phase zero and right phase twelve skip this read.
Twenty-four spray glyphs: twelve left phases then twelve right phases. The previous spray is erased before drawing the next; zero entries end the visible spray.
Right-drill phase values 12..23 index this alias and therefore reach $788F-$789A. The bytes before that real erasure table belong to the spray table.
Twelve staged brick-erasure shapes. Left phase 0..11 uses this base; right phase 12..23 indexes the alias $7883+phase to reach the same twelve shapes.

When scripted controls are polled, any new key or port-2 fire terminates demonstration control, clears alive and leaves one life. Otherwise read a command/duration pair through $55/$56 when the previous duration is zero. Low command nibble selects the primary action, high nibble the secondary; decrement duration once per poll. Gravity and pending-drill updates bypass this poll, freezing duration and deferring its abort check. A stored zero duration underflows to $FF and lasts 256 polls; it is not a stream terminator.

Six authored nibble actions: up, left, down, right, drill-right, drill-left. Both demo-command nibbles index this base unchecked. Index six, present in the embedded command stream, reads opcode $AD at $78EF and supplies an unrecognized action. Indexes seven through fifteen read the following instruction bytes.

Demo mode uses the scripted pair stream. Live modes consume the IRQ key latch, search the game-control RTS directory and dispatch matching commands. Other keys become movement actions in keyboard mode; joystick mode reads the active-low port-2 bits.

Increment lives, displayed level and physical room index, clear alive to reuse the next-room path, and clear high-score eligibility. The lives increment here is an unguarded eight-bit increment, unlike award_extra_life.
Increment lives but undo a zero result to saturate at 255. Redraw MEN, clear high-score eligibility and resume control polling.
Retained entry that increments difficulty cycle and lives and clears alive. It is absent from the eleven game-control directory entries; no ordinary key dispatch reaches it.
Consume new-key latches until raw Run/Stop code $3F appears, then resume control polling. IRQ sound and keyboard scanning continue while movement is paused.
Jump to the high-score/title return path at $61D2, abandoning the active run.
Clear alive so the ordinary death/life-decrement path runs.
Store $CA as the joystick selector and immediately poll controls again.
Store $CB as the keyboard selector and immediately poll controls again.
Reduce the IRQ pacing threshold by one down to three; lower thresholds require fewer timer ticks between main-loop passes.
Increase the pacing threshold by one up to eight; then return to the same control poll.
Complement the reveal-animation flag at $1321. It affects the next room construction, rather than movement within the room.
Complement $1339. Joystick fire XORs this option with signed runner facing to choose the drill side.

Fire takes precedence and selects a drill side from facing XOR drill polarity. Without fire, choose down before up as primary and right before left as secondary. If the vertical action is blocked, runner input tries the horizontal component.
Eleven raw key-latch codes followed by zero, paired with the eleven RTS dispatch words. These select skip, extra life, pause, restart, abandon, input mode, speed, reveal and drill polarity.
Eleven little-endian handler addresses minus one; read_controls pushes the selected word then RTS enters the handler. The difficulty-advance routine at $7955 is separate from this directory.
High-byte partner of the eleven game-control RTS words. Its indexed loads pair with the low-byte base at $7A1C.
Convert runner column/row and fine offsets into pixel coordinates, then translate its animation phase through runner_animation_glyphs. Return glyph A and drawing X/Y.

Only fine-X=fine-Y=2 can collect backing-map gold tile seven. Clear vulnerability for this pass, sample raster positions to rewrite four queued note pitches, and enqueue the effect. The continuation clears gold from the backing map and work bitmap, restores display bits, decreases remaining gold and adds packed-BCD250; the runner marker in the dynamic map remains.
Four duration/pitch/harmony/envelope events and a zero-duration terminator read by enqueue_inline_music. Raster samples rewrite the pitch bytes at $7A95,$7A99,$7A9D,$7AA1; execution resumes at $7AA5.
Mutable pitch byte of gold-effect event 1. The pickup routine writes an accepted raster-line sample here before the inline queue reader consumes the four events.
Mutable pitch byte of gold-effect event 2. The pickup routine writes an accepted raster-line sample here before the inline queue reader consumes the four events.
Mutable pitch byte of gold-effect event 3. The pickup routine writes an accepted raster-line sample here before the inline queue reader consumes the four events.
Mutable pitch byte of gold-effect event 4. The pickup routine writes an accepted raster-line sample here before the inline queue reader consumes the four events.

After the inline music, decrement remaining gold and replace the backing-map collectible with blank. Clear its work-bitmap glyph, restore display bits beneath the runner, then add250 points. The dynamic runner marker is retained.
Advance runner frame $07 within the inclusive range supplied by A and X. Wrap to the lower frame when the increment passes the upper bound.

Resolve runner glyph/coordinates and draw through the sprite path. A reported player/guard VIC contact clears alive only when this pass retains vulnerability; a centered gold pickup has cleared that flag.
Move horizontal fine offset one step toward two. Any change checks centered gold; equal-to-center returns unchanged.
Move vertical fine offset one step toward two and check gold after changing it. Used when entering horizontal movement or drilling.

Clear the drill flag and dynamic-map brick at column X one row below the runner, draw the open hole in both bitmaps and erase the spray above it. The backing map retains brick terrain. Search timer slots0..29 for the first zero, record the cell and set180 updates; if all thirty are occupied the already-opened cell receives no refill timer.

Rotate one of three mask bytes selected during room setup. For each set bit, call update_next_guard, whose index rotates through the guards. Stop early if the runner dies; masks encode update counts, not guard identities.

Twenty-one three-byte masks, each set bit requesting one rotating guard update. Eleven aligned schedule offsets use the first eleven triplets; late-cycle out-of-bounds directory reads select unaligned masks and can reach the following animation table.
Address alias for the second byte of each guard-schedule triplet. Setup reads three successive bytes from the selected offset; each is a mask of rotating update requests.
Address alias for the third mask byte of the selected schedule. The following triplets and late-cycle table aliases are covered by the schedule description at $7B83.
Sixteen glyph indexes for guard standing, walking, climbing and falling frames. render_guard indexes these with its local animation phase.

Rotate the one-based guard index, load its local actor fields, decrement positive trap/escape state and handle respawn delay. Test terrain support and falling, trap in an open brick cell for 75 points, and restore carried gold above a hole when possible. Supported guards dispatch their chosen direction through guard_direction_returns.

For remaining positive trap states 7..12, erase the guard, select a fine-X phase from the overlapping-base wiggle lookup, redraw and save its fields. Smaller states enter normal route choice, which can climb out of the hole.
High byte of JSR at $7D6C is also the lookup base for the escape wiggle. Runtime indexes 7..12 land in the six real data bytes at $7D75-$7D7A, beyond the remaining instructions.
Six fine-X phases 2,1,2,3,2,1 read by escape state values 7..12 through base $7D6E. That base lies inside an instruction; the reachable table begins here.
Call choose_guard_direction, double its 0..4 code, push the selected return word and RTS to stay/left/right/up/down. The pushed word is the handler address minus one.
Five RTS targets minus one, indexed by direction 0..4: save/stay, left, right, up, down. This dispatch reaches the guard movement routines that static call tracing misses.
High-byte base paired with guard_direction_returns to push a direction handler address minus one.

For a blocked upward guard move, restore the positive trap-state counter decremented earlier by incrementing it again. Zero or negative carrying states remain unchanged, then the local actor fields are saved. Other blocked movement handlers save directly.

Center the guard horizontally, climb by one fine-Y phase and cycle climbing glyphs. At a row crossing, attempt carried-gold release, restore the vacated dynamic cell from backing terrain (open brick becomes blank), write guard marker eight in the new dynamic cell and test runner marker nine before saving.

Move the guard downward through five fine-Y phases, respecting bottom bounds and blocking dynamic terrain/guards. At a row crossing, release carried gold when its counter permits, restore the previous dynamic cell from backing terrain, test runner contact and write the new guard marker before drawing and saving.

Step fine-X left, center fine-Y and cycle leftward frames. At a cell crossing, attempt carried-gold release, restore the previous dynamic cell from backing terrain (open brick becomes blank), enter the neighboring dynamic cell, test runner marker nine and store guard marker eight.

Step fine-X right, center fine-Y and cycle rightward frames. At a cell crossing, attempt carried-gold release, restore the vacated dynamic cell from backing terrain (open brick becomes blank), test runner marker nine in the new cell and store guard marker eight. Draw and save the rotating guard's fields.

A guard with positive trap state in backing brick requests up. On the runner row, a direct chase scan accepts ladders/bars or supporting backing terrain below; this shortcut does not reject same-row walls, which the movement handlers later block. Otherwise evaluate the current column, then left candidates from the left limit inward, then right candidates from the right limit inward. Strictly lower costs preserve that scan order on ties.

Scan candidate columns from the left walk/drop limit inward toward the guard, excluding the guard's own column. At each candidate, test downward routes before ladder-up routes. A strictly lower cost sets left as the first move; equal-cost candidates preserve the earlier, farther-left choice.

Scan candidate columns from the right walk/drop limit inward toward the guard, excluding its own column, after the left scan. Test downward before upward routes and retain only strictly lower costs; ties cannot override earlier current-column or left candidates, or the earlier farther-right candidate on this side.

Evaluate downward then ladder-up routes at the guard's current column. Score each returned row and retain only a strictly cheaper result, setting direction down or up in $2B. This runs before either lateral candidate scan.

Given candidate row A and column X, same-runner-row cost is the absolute lateral distance from the guard column. A candidate above the runner costs vertical gap+100; below costs gap+200. This local ranking chooses ladder/drop approaches rather than a global shortest path.

Scan upward while the current backing cell is a ladder, stopping at the top or a useful side exit at/above the runner row. Side exits use bars in the candidate row or brick/concrete/ladder support below it. Return the candidate row in A; callers do not use carry as a route-validity flag.

Scan downward until backing brick/concrete below or the bottom limit, returning the candidate row for route cost. Nonblank current cells permit side-exit tests: the left side tests a current-row bar or backing support below. The right-side bar read reuses the pointer left by that test, so it can inspect the row below before testing below-row support. At row fifteen the next-row directory read precedes final bottom handling and aliases $8D76/$8D96.

Find left/right dynamic-map walk limits. Brick/concrete and bounds stop the scan; a ladder/bar or backing support below permits continuation. The first unsupported edge cell is included in the saved limit so the route search can evaluate a drop there.
Convert local guard cell coordinates plus fine phases into drawing X/Y and translate its animation index through guard_animation_glyphs.

With both fine phases centered and carrying/trap state nonnegative, collect backing-map gold. Set carrying state to $FF minus the rotating seed, clear only the backing collectible (the dynamic guard marker remains), clear the work glyph and restore display background. Remaining-gold count is retained.

Increment a negative carrying state on cell crossings. When it reaches zero, drop gold only into a blank backing-map cell, draw it into work and display bitmaps, and let the movement caller restore the vacated dynamic cell from that backing value. A blocked drop returns the state to $FF for another crossing.
Advance the local guard animation index within the lower/upper bounds supplied in A/X, wrapping to the lower bound.
Move the local guard fine-X phase one step toward two and invoke centered gold pickup after a change. Fine-Y is handled separately by center_guard_fine_y.
Move the guard vertical phase one step toward two and invoke centered gold pickup after a change.
Store local column,row,carrying/trap state,fine-X,fine-Y,animation and facing into their parallel arrays at $1260,$1268,$1270,$1278,$1280,$1288,$1290, indexed by the one-based current guard.
Load the same seven parallel guard arrays into zero-page local fields $15-$1B for the rotating current guard index.

Update guard respawn delays, rotate the carrying/respawn-column seed over 28 columns and scan timer indexes 30 down to zero (allocation uses 0..29). Decrement active timers; redraw partial closure at 20 and 10 remaining, and restore brick at zero. A runner in the cell dies; a guard is hidden and relocated for respawn, awarding another 75 points.

Tick nonzero guard respawn delays, draw appearance stages at19 and10, and try to restore the guard at zero. Require a blank dynamic-map destination; otherwise retain delay one and retry. A successful respawn writes dynamic guard marker eight, removes appearance graphics, restores normal state and enables its sprite.
Six mask bytes, index zero unused and indexes 1..5 setting hardware sprite bits 2,3,4,6,7. Respawn ORs these into $D015.

Six disable-mask entries: unused index-zero sentinel $00, followed by $FB, $F7, $EF, $BF, and $7F, the inverse masks for guards 1..5 in sprite slots 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7. A guard buried by a closing hole is hidden until its respawn cell clears.
Clear display then work bitmaps; execution falls into draw_status_bar for the default status rendering.

Draw the status border and SCORE/MEN/LEVEL text in bitmap $2000 or $4000. A glyph checksum and disk-probe flag affect a self-modifying glyph-source operand; draw lives, level and the lowest seven score digits.
Low store-address byte of STA at $870E, advanced by eight to draw the bitmap border. Carry increments its high byte; both reset after the loop. The following mirrored code handles the work bitmap.
High store-address byte paired with status_display_border_operand at $870F. The border loop increments it on low-byte carry and restores $3B before returning to the status text path.
Low store-address byte in the work-bitmap border STA. The loop advances by eight with carry into its high byte and restores its starting address afterward.
High store-address byte of the work-bitmap border STA at $8751, paired with low byte $8752. Carry increments it during border drawing, then the code restores $5B before printing status text.
Inline high-bit PETSCII text read by print_inline_text at $877A: SCORE        MEN    LEVEL. Zero terminates it, and execution resumes at $879A.

After the inline status text, fold70 bytes from the disk-probe page using ADC with cleared carry and XOR one. draw_status_bar has patched the ADC source high byte to $8E; an unexpected checksum increments the glyph-source page immediate at $8B01. Restore the ADC source high byte to $A8 and render MEN, LEVEL and SCORE.

Low address operand of ADC at $879F, set to $11 by each disk probe. With draw_status_bar's temporary high byte $8E, the70-byte checksum covers $8E11-$8E56, including the mutable probe status arrays. The high byte is restored to $A8 afterward.

High address operand of ADC at $879F. draw_status_bar temporarily sets it to $8E for the disk-probe checksum and restores $A8 afterward; it is distinct from the glyph expansion source-page immediate at $8B01.
Render the binary lives byte as three decimal digits at status column 16, row 16.
Render the displayed-level byte as three decimal digits at status column 25, row 16, sharing the lives conversion/drawing path.

Add packed-BCD A/Y into four little-endian score bytes under decimal mode, propagating carry and discarding overflow beyond eight digits. Clear decimal mode and redraw only the lowest seven digits: the high nibble of the top score byte is not printed.
Convert packed BCD in A into its high and low digit nibbles at $1308/$1309, for score printing.

Repeatedly subtract 100 and 10 from A to produce the three decimal digits at $1307-$1309. Called for editor board-number entry, high-score record level, and the shared lives/displayed-level drawing path. Rank rows print digits directly.
Convert digit A to glyph 59+A. Draw it in the bitmap selected by $51 and advance the logical text column.

Map $C1-$DA to alphabet glyphs 69..94 and the seven accepted high-bit punctuation bytes to glyphs 95..101; $A0 maps to blank glyph zero. Unsupported bytes map to glyph 16. The game font is a bitmap-glyph atlas, not a VIC character set.
Carriage return advances the logical row and resets column. Otherwise translate the byte through text_byte_to_glyph and stamp its glyph into the current work/display bitmap, advancing one cell.
Increment the text row and reset the logical column to zero. This is the newline branch of print_text_byte.

Pull the caller return address, read a zero-terminated high-bit PETSCII string immediately after the JSR and draw it using the custom glyph mapper. Push the terminator address back so RTS continues after the text rather than executing it.

Set the interrupt-disable flag, write voice-one frequency high byte $60, wait with a CPU counting loop, clear that high byte and execute CLI. Menu errors use this beep; CLI enables interrupts rather than restoring the caller's prior interrupt mask.
Alternate the current cell glyph with a blank/solid cursor while polling input_seen. Restore its glyph and return as soon as joystick motion, fire or a new key is present.
Return carry set for any active-low port-2 direction or fire bit, or a nonzero IRQ key latch at $1328; otherwise carry clear. This is the start/cursor-wait test, not the movement decoder.
Save glyph A and select display bitmap $2000. Convert column/row at $4F/$50 through cell_to_pixel; eligible actors use sprites while terrain/text composes eleven masked bitmap scanlines.
Save glyph A and select preserved work bitmap $4000, then share cell conversion and masked glyph drawing. Gold/brick changes update this background before visible restoration or overlay.
Four left and four right preserve masks for glyphs at the four horizontal phases. Masked bitmap stamping retains neighboring cell bits.
The four right-edge preservation masks, paired with the left-edge masks at $8A17.

Expand the glyph mask, then erase it from display bitmap $2000 by combining (display AND inverse mask) OR the full matching work-bitmap byte. The normal horizontal phases0..3 take the two-byte scanline path. A retained three-byte path tests for phase at least5, beyond prepare_horizontal_phase's returned range.
Resolve the actor/glyph rendering path, build the horizontal-phase mask and OR it into the display bitmap, retaining other background bits.

A glyph index in $23 selects each of 22 row tables spaced $68 bytes apart from $A800. The horizontal phase picks paired lookup pages at $A000-$A7FF. Combine two patterns per scanline into the 33-byte scratch mask at $005B.

Immediate page byte of LDA #$A8 at $8B00, used to initialize glyph source pointer high byte $0E. The source starts at $A800 with low byte zero. A failed disk-probe checksum increments this immediate, moving the glyph source to the next256-byte page.

High page operand of LDA at $8B1B, patched from $A0,$A2,$A4,$A6 by horizontal phase. Its paired expansion page is the next high byte. The glyph-row pointer, rather than these lookup pages, advances by $68 per encoded pattern row.

High-byte operand of the overflow lookup LDA at $8B20. Horizontal phase chooses its page as the first expansion page plus one; the following combine/store code assembles the remaining glyph scanlines.
High operand of LDA at $8B37, patched to the same first expansion page as $8B1D. This second encoded pattern combines its first byte with the prior pattern overflow to assemble the middle mask byte.
High operand of LDA at $8B3E, patched to the second expansion page selected for the horizontal phase. Its value forms the third mask byte before the row pointer advances by $68.
The four high bytes $A0,$A2,$A4,$A6 select paired low/high expansion pages in expand_glyph_scanlines.

In play modes, recognized actor glyphs map to a sprite slot and its 33-byte shape buffer; position registers and X-high bits are updated. Reading $D01E yields player/guard contact. Pulling the caller return address skips the bitmap path after a sprite draw; editor mode uses the bitmap path.
Interleaved set/clear masks for the eight VIC sprite slots. draw_actor_as_sprite uses its even register offset to update $D010 without changing other sprites.
Clear-mask base of the interleaved sprite X-high masks; even hardware-register offsets select the corresponding slot mask.
57 entries classify low-numbered glyphs for the actor sprite path. $FF forces bitmap rendering; zero keeps the requested actor glyph, while positive entries substitute the indicated sprite glyph.

Save the selector in A across expansion of the glyph indexed by zero-page byte $23, using horizontal phase $21&3. A=0 selects the player; any nonzero A selects the current one-based guard from $131F. Patch the sprite destination operands and copy33 mask bytes with Y=32..0. Return X as twice the selected VIC sprite slot.
STA absolute,Y used by write_actor_sprite_shape. Its low/high address operands at $8C19/$8C1A are patched to the selected $0C00/$0D00 sprite buffer, and Y copies offsets32 down to zero.
Low address byte of sprite_shape_store, patched from actor_sprite_buffer_lows. The 33-byte store loop uses the selected player/guard shape buffer.
High address byte of sprite_shape_store, selecting page $0C or $0D from actor_sprite_buffer_highs.
Low-byte destinations for player plus five guard sprite shapes: $00,$40,$80,$C0,$00,$40. High bytes and hardware slots are in the following directories.
High-byte partners $0C,$0C,$0C,$0C,$0D,$0D for the six 64-byte actor sprite buffers.
VIC slots 0,2,3,4,6,7 for the player and five guards. The omitted hardware slots remain outside the actor enable masks.

Convert column X and row Y through fixed tables. Horizontal coordinate is10+5*column in multicolour pixels; room rows0..15 use vertical pixel11*row, while status row16 is specially placed at181. Return X/Y.
Vertical cell positions: room rows0..15 are0,11,...,165; status row16 is181, leaving a five-pixel gap beyond the room's176-pixel height. Cell conversion indexes this17-byte table.
28 horizontal positions 10+5*column. Each step is five multicolour pixels, hence ten physical screen pixels.

Convert logical column X to its multicolour-pixel position and add the signed fine-X offset selected by the original Y from[-2,-1,0,1,2]. The original Y is saved before cell conversion; return the adjusted coordinate in X.
Signed offsets -2,-1,0,1,2 added to a cell half-pixel coordinate for the five horizontal movement phases.
Convert the cell position and add the fine vertical offset selected by the original X from [-5,-3,0,2,4].
Signed pixel offsets -5,-3,0,2,4 used by runner_vertical_pixel for the five vertical movement phases.

Retained executable helper: index two 30-entry tables with X, preserve the first result on the stack and return it in A with the second in X. No direct call in the primary engine names this entry; its game-facing purpose remains unverified.
Thirty values returned in A by retained_x_conversion_helper. The byte sequence advances over 2..38 with gaps; its independent companion table selects a repeating phase.
Thirty phases returned in X by retained_x_conversion_helper: 2,3,0,1 repeating. These are retained conversion data rather than bitmap rows or cell terrain.
Split horizontal half-pixel X into the phase X modulo four and the aligned bitmap byte offset. Preserve its ninth-bit carry separately for bitmap addressing.

Y selects a row through directories at $8D66/$8D76/$8D86. Return dynamic actor/collision-map pointer $09/$0A and backing terrain/collectible-map pointer $0B/$0C. The28-cell rows have a four-byte page gap before row nine.
Clear the horizontal offset and carry, then share bitmap_address_for_row.
Use generated row lookup pages $0E00/$0F00 and the saved horizontal offset to form bitmap pointer $0F/$10. The bitmap base is selected by $24.
Convert byte-column X into X*8 with its carry for the following bitmap address calculation.
Resolve the current scanline plus aligned horizontal offset in bitmap $2000, and return the matching $4000 address through XOR of the bitmap-base bits.
Disable all sprites and zero pages $2000-$3FFF through the indirect fill loop. Shares the fill machinery with clear_work_bitmap.
Zero pages $4000-$5FFF through the common bitmap fill loop, using a different start and end page than clear_display_bitmap.

RTS ending the common bitmap fill loop. Its end page is passed in X ($40 for display, $60 for work) and compared against pointer high byte $10 at $8D61; this address is an opcode, not a mutable operand.

Sixteen shared low bytes for the dynamic and backing maps'28-cell rows. Rows0..8 are contiguous; row nine starts a new page at low byte zero, leaving four unused bytes after row eight. The two high-byte directories select the map.

One-row-forward alias of grid_row_pointer_lows. A row-fifteen next-row access runs into byte $8D76 of the following directory; scan_guard_downward_exit can perform that access before applying its final bottom bound.
Final row-pointer low byte ($A8) for row fifteen. It pairs with high byte $09 for dynamic cells or $0B for backing cells. A next-row lookup beyond it aliases the following high-byte directory.

High-byte partners for sixteen dynamic actor/collision rows at $0800/$0900. Guards and runner markers occupy this map; moving guards restore vacated cells from backing terrain. Row nine starts at $0900, after a four-byte gap.
One-row-forward high-byte alias for the dynamic actor/collision grid, paired with $8D67 in below-row tests.

High-byte partners for sixteen backing terrain/collectible rows at $0A00/$0B00. This map retains terrain beneath actors and brick beneath open holes; gold pickup/drop and exit reveal update it. Row nine starts at $0B00 after a four-byte gap.
One-row-forward high-byte alias for the backing terrain/collectible grid, paired with the shared low-byte alias in support/drop tests. A row-fifteen lookup aliases code byte $A9 at $8D96.

When remaining gold is zero, try each recorded exit cell in descending order. Blank backing terrain becomes ladder three and is drawn; the dynamic cell is also changed only if blank, preserving any actor marker. Nonblank backing cells remain pending. After every backing exit is activated, remaining-gold/exit state becomes $FF.
One initialized zero byte used as the descending exit-ladder index by activate_hidden_exit_ladders.
Wait for a nonzero IRQ key latch, clear it and return the raw key code in A. Its decoded caller is pause_until_runstop at $795F; editor confirmation uses the flashing-cursor input path.

Request fixed sector two on tracks 02,01,34,35 and branch on the resulting DOS status digits. Black enters at $8E11 for all checks; Gray starts at $8E32 with prior results prefilled. The final probe changes a glyph-checksum source operand.
Four mutable first DOS status digits. The Black image loads zeros; Gray's IT file preloads ASCII first digits2,0,2,0, providing prior probe results before its entry at the fourth request.
Four mutable second DOS status digits paired with probe_first_status_digits. Their combination determines each disk-probe branch.

X/Y are the two ASCII track digits, and A selects a result slot. Issue U1 for fixed sector two on drive eight, read its two status digits into probe arrays, close channels and compare their OR with ASCII zero. Set the checksum-source low operand to $11.
Direct-buffer filename # followed by zero-terminated U1 command for buffer five, unit zero, a mutable two-digit ASCII track and fixed sector two. probe_sector_error writes only the two track digits.
Start of the zero-terminated U1 probe command, following the # direct-buffer filename. Mutable command digits select the intentional probe reads.
Two mutable ASCII track digits in the U1 command. The Black probe requests tracks02,01,34,35, always sector two; Gray calls only the fourth request and supplies earlier status results from its file.
Mutable ASCII units digit paired with the probe track tens byte. Fixed sector two follows it in the direct-buffer U1 command.

Repeat eleven wrappers that each draw a fourteen-row game-over ornament. The software delay increments once per wrapper draw; repeat expansion/contraction sequences until the delay reaches at least100, then draw six final stages. Fire or a new key can discard the animation return and exit early.
Game-over banner step 1: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 1, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F24 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 2: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 2, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F35 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 3: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 3, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F46 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 4: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 4, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F57 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 5: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 5, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F68 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 6: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 6, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F79 and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 7: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 7, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F8A and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 8: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 8, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8F9B and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 9: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 9, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8FAC and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 10: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 10, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8FBD and never executes these bytes.
Game-over banner step 11: call draw_banner_rows with fourteen inline pattern indexes. The callee consumes this wrapper return and returns directly to animate_game_over_banner.

Fourteen pattern indexes for banner step 11, read after the JSR to draw_banner_rows. The callee removes this wrapper return address, so it returns to the caller of $8FCE and never executes these bytes.

Eleven12-byte horizontal row patterns for the game-over ornament. Each inline index selects one pattern; the renderer reads offsets14..25 from a pointer based fourteen bytes before it, shifts each byte right once and writes bitmap byte columns14..25 on that scanline.
Eleven little-endian pointers equal to each 12-byte pattern start minus fourteen. The renderer uses Y=14..25 through a rewritten absolute operand to reach that pattern.
High-byte base of the eleven banner pointers, paired with $9063 to rewrite the banner LDA operand.

Remove the wrapper return address and consume its fourteen inline pattern indexes for bitmap scanlines81..94. Each index patches a12-byte horizontal pattern source; shift bytes right once and write bitmap byte columns14..25. Increment software delay once after all fourteen rows. Fire/new key discards the animation's return and returns carry set to its caller.

LDA absolute,Y whose operands $90A7/$90A8 select a pattern pointer fourteen bytes before its data. Read Y=14..25, shift each byte right and copy it across bitmap byte columns14..25 on the current scanline.

Low address operand of banner_pattern_load, rewritten from banner_pattern_pointers. The continuation copies twelve shifted source bytes across the current bitmap scanline, then advances the inline row stream and handles delay/input after all fourteen rows.
High operand byte paired with banner_source_low_operand. It selects the pattern source page for the self-modified LDA.
Initial zero delay byte, set to one by animate_game_over_banner and incremented once per complete call to draw_banner_rows. The animation tests it against 100 before the final six steps.
Increment the banner inline-data pointer $0D/$0E by one, propagating carry.

If a previous room exists, sweep decreasing circle radii164..1 to erase display nibbles. Refresh MEN and LEVEL, then sweep radii1..163 to OR masked nibbles from the new work bitmap into the display. The caller's transition option chooses this routine or a direct bitmap copy.

Initialize an integer midpoint-circle calculation centered at X=160 of 320 bit positions and Y=88 for radius $3D. Iterate signed decision error and symmetric coordinate pairs, plotting through plot_iris_octants; byte columns and three-bit offsets change on each step. Nibble masks make its visible multicolour boundary coarser than single bits.
Split the 16-bit pixel coordinate A:X into a byte-column Y and low three-bit position A for circle drawing, using rotations through the saved high byte.

Plot eight symmetric circle points, clipping byte coordinates to Y0..175 and X0..39. Shrink mode masks off one display nibble. Reveal mode masks that nibble from the work bitmap and ORs it into display, relying on the shrink/cleared display state for replacement. Four-bit masks make the boundary advance in groups of two multicolour pixels.

Eight shrink masks: four $0F values then four $F0 values. Bit positions 0..3 select one preserved nibble and 4..7 the other; each nibble contains two multicolour pixels. The reveal mask base overlaps at $93B3.
Eight reveal masks starting with four $F0 bytes then four $0F bytes. This table overlaps the shrink-mask table and the four following retained bytes.

Four retained $0F bytes immediately before the embedded symbol records. The eight-entry reveal-mask read through base $93B3 overlaps these bytes: bit-position indexes zero through three select $F0, and indexes four through seven select $0F.

Retained assembler-style name/address records begin with truncated ameover, followed by gameovr2, ban1..ban11, bandat0..bandat10 and banner helpers. Complete address words name live routines/tables at $8EC4..$90EB. Known banner dispatch uses the live pointer directories; no direct reader of this record format was identified.
Initial motif countdown nine. advance_motif_cycle decrements through zero and changes transposition on the tenth call, then reloads nine.
Initial completion-motif offset two semitones.
